references.text: Jacob bought the plot of land at Shechem, which connects him to this place and the well that the Samaritan woman refers to ([ref:1 Mos 33:19|Genesis 33:19]).
Jacob gave Joseph the plot of land at Shechem as a special inheritance, confirming Jacob's connection to this area and the well ([ref:1 Mos 48:22|Genesis 48:22]).

The Jews ask Jesus a similar question: "Are you greater than our father Abraham?" – the same kind of challenge that the Samaritan woman raises against Jesus by comparing him with Jacob ([ref:Joh 8:53|John 8:53]).

Background to the conversation: Jesus came to Jacob's well at Sychar, near the plot of land Jacob gave to Joseph. The woman's question in verse 12 refers back to this well and its connection to Jacob ([ref:Joh 4:5-6|John 4:5-6]).

Joseph's bones were buried in Shechem, on the plot of land that Jacob had bought. This underscores the historical connection between Jacob, his descendants, and this place ([ref:Jos 24:32|Joshua 24:32]).
Jesus answers the woman's question indirectly by declaring that whoever drinks the water he gives will never thirst again – showing that he is greater than Jacob ([ref:Joh 4:14|John 4:14]).
The prophecy about drawing water with joy from the wells of salvation points to the living water Jesus offers, which is far greater than what Jacob gave ([ref:Jes 12:3|Isaiah 12:3]).

Jesus deserves greater honor than Moses, just as the builder of a house has more honor than the house itself – the same "greater than" theme found in the Samaritan woman's question ([ref:Heb 3:3|Hebrews 3:3]).
